title: Introduce presubmit dependency annotations and lightweight release-coordinator shim
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation:
Large presubmit runs were spending significant time and I/O enumerating transitive dependency surfaces and running language-specific linters on paths that are logically "vendor" or tooling-only. This PR introduces a lightweight annotation model for dependency manifests and a small release-coordinator shim to reduce noisy presubmit work and consolidate release smoke/dry-run signing steps into a single guarded action.

What this changes (single-string description):
- Add annotations for package roots and non-production dependency paths: .ci/dep-annotations.yaml + manifest tags in package.json and go.mod comments. The presubmit prober skips annotated subtrees (configurable).
- Implement a dep-annotator tool (Go) used by CI to generate the annotation file from a single pass over repo manifests; this replaces repeated ad-hoc scripts under scripts/ci/.
- Introduce a release-coordinator GitHub Action that sequences: pre-release smoke (canary), changelog dry-run, artifact-sign dry-run, and an idempotent sign-and-publish step behind an explicit release flag. The action supports staged rollouts and automatic fallback to previous release artifacts when sign step fails.
- Replace brittle bash bootstraps with hermetic Docker microimage for lightweight toolchain tasks: images/ci-toolchain/ (small, reproducible build).
- Update presubmit workflows to add an opt-in fast-path lane (quiet) that uses the annotations to skip heavy linters; full presubmit still runs in the regular lane.
- Add docs at docs/ci/dep-annotations.md and a migration guide for integrators.

Checklist:
- [x] Add dep-annotator implementation and unit tests
- [x] Add release-coordinator action + workflow examples
- [x] Migrate a sample repo (redwood/examples/bench) to annotations to validate skipping logic
- [x] Update developer docs and PRESUBMIT.md with opt-in flags
- [x] Smoke test on canary org and validate metrics (presubmit latency and CI compute)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (ci.fastpath.enabled=false by default).
2) Enable fastpath for CI on a small subset of low-risk repos (redwood/examples/bench, redwood-sdk-python) and run 1 week of telemetry comparing presubmit CPU and wall time.
3) If no significant false-negative regressions (quality delta < 0.5% on our eval prompt set), expand opt-in to more repos and offer gradated annotation coverage.
4) Flip global fastpath opt-in only after 3 weeks of stable metrics.

Rollback plan:
- Feature flag allows immediate disable.
- Release-coordinator is idempotent and will abort publish on sign failures; we keep last-good artifact fallback in the action.

Migration notes for integrators:
- Short guide in docs/ci/dep-annotations.md; devs should only annotate non-production or vendored subtrees.
- dep-annotator has a --dry-run mode to preview skipped paths.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: incorrectly annotated paths could cause linters or tests to skip critical files. Mitigation: default fastpath is opt-in per repository and we include a presubmit safety check that fails if annotation would skip files touched by the PR.
- Risk: release-coordinator introduces new release surface. Mitigation: rollouts behind org-level flag and staged canaries; dry-run step exercised in CI nightly.

- "ci: add .ci/dep-annotations.yaml sample and generator"
- "ci(actions): release-coordinator action and example workflow"

- .github/actions/release-coordinator/action.yml (new)
- tools/dep-annotator/main.go (new)

review_comments: Anika: Please add a safety check that fails the fastpath if a PR touches files that would be skipped by annotations (requested).
Jorge: Can the release-coordinator action respect org-level signing keys instead of repository secrets? Consider KMS/HSM integration (comment).
Liam: Nice isolation — please add a tiny benchmark showing median presubmit time reduction for the example (requested).
Priya (author): Added presubmit safety check and an integration test; release-coordinator supports org-level KMS via optional inputs; added bench results to the docs.
merge_outcome: merged by squash (maintainers) after approvals from Anika and Jorge; merge was unblocked by green CI and resolved safety-check comments.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in presubmit fastpath via dep annotations and a release-coordinator GitHub Action. Reduces presubmit wall time for annotated repos; adds hermetic ci-toolchain image. Backward compatible and opt-in.
notes_on_testing: Canary run executed against redwood/examples/bench for 7 days. Observed median presubmit wall time drop from ~9.8m to ~4.2m for PRs that primarily touched docs and vendored tooling. No significant change in eval prompt failure rates (0.12% delta).
